svg.title: Why DRAM needs refresh, and how Row Hammer disturbs neighboring rows
svg.desc: Animated: DRAM cell charge leaks and is restored by refresh; repeated access to an aggressor row makes weak cells in neighboring victim rows lose their bits; early neighbor refresh prevents it. Values are illustrative.
svg.text: Why DRAM needs refresh, and what Row Hammer does
Each bit is charge in a tiny capacitor (cells shown store a 1). Showing 5 rows x 8 cells of a much larger array.

g.text: Each cell is a tiny capacitor that
Refresh reads every row and writes
it back once per window (64 ms,
and the weakest cross the threshold
before the next refresh: their bits
The memory controller or the DRAM
the neighbor rows early, so the
Normal rows keep the usual window.

svg.text: Illustrative: 4 s of animation = one 64 ms window; leak rates and the hammer count are example values, not measurements.
